name: Basra
summary: Middle Eastern fishing card game where players capture table cards by matching rank or summing values, with special jacks.
rules_text: Use 52 cards for 2 players or 4 in fixed partnerships opposite. Dealer deals 4 cards each anticlockwise and 4 face up to floor, re-dealing any jacks or 7 of diamonds initially on floor. Players alternate playing one card to floor. If rank matches a floor card, you capture that card plus your played card. If your numeral equals sum of some floor numerals (Ace=1) you capture those plus your card; you may make both types at once and capture multiple matching ranks. Queens and kings only match same rank. Captures go face down to your pile. Playing Jack captures all floor cards, leaving it empty, but not a Basra unless floor was single Jack (variant). 7 of diamonds also captures all floor cards; if floor numerals total <=10 it is a Basra. Basra = clearing floor, scores 10 bonus, mark by turning capturing card face up. If played to empty floor, Jack or 7 stays. Last capture takes remaining floor cards without bonus. Most cards scores 30, aces and jacks 1 each, 2 of clubs 2, 10 of diamonds 3, plus Basra bonuses. First to 101 wins.
rating_reason: Specific fishing card game, turn-based, hidden hands, strategic captures.
